what: The hard cases (examples/hard_cases.json), asked in the app one after another (scripts/hard_cases.mjs)
rule: a count must equal the key, a measure must be within 2% of it, a refusal is right where one is due; 'no key' means nobody worked the answer out by hand

rows.asked: Given one size only, work out the rest
rows.label: Only a door's width is given: the hall's floor area
rows.question: The double door between the Multi-Purpose Hall and the Store is 1.7 m wide. Using only that as the scale, what is the floor area of the Multi-Purpose Hall, in m²?

expect.basis: the same hall measured against the sheet's scale bar (245.0 m²). Not an independent key: no figure for the hall is printed on the sheet

rows.engine: Measured on the sheet, in its own pixels
rows.reason: 17.77 m × 13.74 m = 244.14 m². Measured on the sheet: each side of the room was moved onto the inner face of its wall, and the lengths were read against the size the question gives (double door between Multi-Purpose Hall and Store: 1.7 m = 86 px on the sheet).

rows.asked: Given one size only, work out the rest
rows.label: The same door as the ruler: metres of baseboard
rows.question: The double door between the Multi-Purpose Hall and the Store is 1.7 m wide. Using only that, how many metres of baseboard does the Multi-Purpose Hall need?

expect.basis: the same baseboard measured against the sheet's scale bar (50.4 m). Not an independent key

rows.engine: Measured on the sheet, in its own pixels
rows.reason: 2 × (17.77 m + 13.74 m) − 12.71 m of door openings = 50.31 m. Measured on the sheet: each side of the room was moved onto the inner face of its wall, and the lengths were read against the size the question gives (double door between Multi-Purpose Hall and Store: 1.7 m = 86 px on the sheet). 8 door openings left out.

rows.label: A size that contradicts the sheet: it must refuse
rows.question: The Multi-Purpose Hall is 25 m long. Using only that, what is its floor area in m²?

expect.basis: by the sheet's own scale bar the hall is about 17.8 m long; a stated size more than 5% away from the sheet's scale is refused

rows.engine: Measured on the sheet, in its own pixels
rows.reason: the size given in the question (length of the Multi-Purpose Hall: 25 m) makes the sheet 36.0 px per metre, and the sheet's own scale bar (20 m = 1,010 px) makes it 50.5: they are 29% apart, so nothing is measured. Check which thing the size belongs to

rows.label: Baseboards of a hall, measured on the sheet
rows.question: How many linear metres of baseboard are needed in the Multi-Purpose Hall?

expect.basis: no key: nobody measured the hall by hand. Earlier runs gave 50.4 m twice

rows.engine: Measured on the sheet, in its own pixels
rows.reason: 2 × (17.80 m + 13.76 m) − 12.73 m of door openings = 50.4 m. Measured on the sheet: each side of the room was moved onto the inner face of its wall, and the lengths were read against the scale bar (20 m = 1,010 px). 8 door openings left out.
rows.verdict: no key to hold it against

rows.label: Every door of a school, boxed tile by tile
rows.question: How many doors are shown on this floor plan?

expect.basis: no key: nobody counted the doors by hand. Earlier runs gave 118 (5 more doubtful) and 122

rows.reason: 113 boxed by the model on 8 tiles of the sheet at full size, in both of two independent passes; merged and counted by the code. 6 more were boxed in only one of the two passes: they are drawn as doubtful and not counted.
rows.verdict: no key to hold it against

rows.asked: Slab area by type, holes taken out
rows.label: The 150 mm slab, less the trenches cut into it
rows.question: What is the area of the 150 mm slab-on-grade in m²?

expect.basis: our key: 6200 × 9950 mm by the printed dimensions, less the two trenches drawn inside the slab

rows.reason: 61.69 m² − 2.41 m² = 59.28 m². 61.69 m² by the printed dimensions. Taken out: MOTOR CONTROL CENTER TRENCH: 4.28 m × 0.41 m = 1.74 m²; PUMP CONTROL PANEL TRENCH: 1.75 m × 0.39 m = 0.68 m². Their size is not printed on this sheet, so each was measured where it is drawn, against a dimension printed on the plan (9950 mm = 1,420 px; both ends moved onto the lines that cross it). Both examiners found them and the measurements agree.

rows.asked: Slab area by type (thickness and bars)
rows.label: The 300 mm slab reinforced with D16 bars
rows.question: What is the area of the 300 mm slab-on-grade reinforced with D16 bars, in m²?

expect.basis: no key. Earlier runs gave between 217.11 and 218.64 m²

rows.label: Circulation area, added up from the sheet's table
rows.question: What is the total circulation area on the second floor, in square feet?

expect.basis: our key: 914 + 913 + 1,403 + 1,240 SF, added by hand from the sheet's table

rows.reason: 914 SF + 913 SF + 1,403 SF + 1,240 SF = 4,470 ft². Computed from 4 figures printed on the sheet. All 4 figures were read again by the program and match. A second, independent working came to the same result.

rows.label: Pumps on a piping plan, found by their tags
rows.question: How many fueling pumps (FP) are shown on this piping plan?

expect.basis: our key: tags FP-1 to FP-5

rows.reason: 5 listed on the sheet by the model, counted by the code; 5 of them are identified by a text printed on the sheet.

rows.label: The size of a header, read off the piping plan
rows.question: What is the diameter of the suction header, in inches?

expect.basis: our key: the printed callout 16" SUCTION HEADER

rows.reason: 16" = 16 in. Computed from 1 figure printed on the sheet. The figure was read again by the program and matches.

rows.asked: An area with a hole in it
rows.label: A corridor around a lift: the lift is cut out
rows.question: What is the net floor area of room 4.15 ('Korridor') in m²?

expect.basis: the dataset's own answer for this question

rows.reason: Room 4.15 ('Korridor'): outline area 13.99 m²; no area is printed in this room to compare with. The outline encloses 17.23 m²; 2 holes inside it (3.24 m²: shafts, columns or rooms of their own) are taken out.

rows.asked: A question in your own words
rows.label: Asked loosely: read by two models, counted by geometry
rows.question: how many toilets are there in the bagno rooms

expect.basis: no key for this wording. The count is the geometry's, in the rooms both readers chose

rows.reason: 5 toilets standing in those rooms: 1.04 Bagno, 1.09 Bagno, 1.14 Bagno, 1.19 Bagno, 1.24 Bagno, 1.27 Bagno. The plan holds 5 on the whole floor.
rows.verdict: no key to hold it against

note: First filmed run of all twelve. Before the reply cap was lowered and failed calls were asked again: the D16 slab question's first model call ran past the 150 s limit (the model thinking in circles until its 16,000-token cap) and the question got no number. Its video was not kept; the video in docs/ is the run of 03:33 UTC.
